_what: Two knobs for the disk-contention A/B. Edit between runs; the app re-reads this file at the start of every cell alignment, so it does NOT need restarting. Every run logs which combination it used.
_cell_alignment_workers: How many HYBES to fit at once (the pool fans over hybes now, not cells). null = the measured default (cpu_count-2, capped at 16 -> 16 on this box). 3 is MEASURED, not guessed, on the real MAZ store at its real 134-hybe shape, cold FOVs, seconds per hybe: 6 workers gave 4.87 (FOV009, 70 cells), 4.00 (FOV010, 64) and 4.37 (FOV011, 61); 3 workers gave 3.60 (FOV013, 100 cells) and 2.53 (FOV014, 51). The two ranges do not overlap, and the 3-worker arm carried MORE cells. Median 4.37 -> 3.07 s/hybe, 1.42x. This storage is bandwidth-bound -- roughly 93% of the work is per-hybe NAS access and 7% is per-cell arithmetic -- so more readers just contend. The same shape showed at 12 hybes (691 ms/cell at 1 worker, 615 at 3, 796 at 6). Nobody has tried 2. THE RIGHT VALUE DEPENDS ON THE EXPERIMENT'S SHAPE, and 3 is not it everywhere. Measured again 2026-09-28 on the real C7 store (S:, 19 non-reference hybes, ~185 cells/FOV, cold, one fresh FOV per arm, localization running alongside so every arm carried the same load): 3 workers 120.3 s (FOV040, 180 cells), 8 workers 88.2 s (FOV039, 189), 16 workers 74.5 s (FOV034, 184), 19 workers 76.8 s (FOV035, 185). Per cell 0.668 -> 0.467 -> 0.405 -> 0.415 s: 16 is 1.65x the 3-worker arm and 19 is no better, which is what the dispatch predicts -- the pool fans over HYBE GROUPS and max_workers is min(n, len(groups)), so 19 hybes is the whole width. The MAZ number is not wrong; the shapes are opposite. MAZ read 134 hybes for 51-100 cells, so reads dominated and readers contended. C7 reads 19 hybes for ~185 cells -- ten times the arithmetic per read -- so the pool is no longer bandwidth-bound and more workers pay. Set this per experiment: few hybes and many cells -> raise it toward the hybe count; many hybes and few cells -> lower it. Not covered: a GUI session (every arm here was headless, so nothing measured how much the window is starved at 16).
_child_io_priority: Where pool children sit in the disk queue: 'verylow' (default), 'low', or 'normal' to switch it off. This one is GLOBAL -- it reaches every pool in the app, not just cell alignment -- so do not run an ingestion or a tracing job during an arm.
_the_four_arms: 1. {"cell_alignment_workers": null, "child_io_priority": "normal"}   <- the old behaviour, the control
_reading_the_log: Each run logs one line: settings -> the pool actually built | N passes in T s (rate) | GUI blocked X% of the run, lag median/p95/worst. Compare 'rate' (did the alignment get slower?) against 'blocked %' (did the window get usable?). A run whose pool shape differs from the others -- 'per-hybe' instead of 'across-cells' -- is NOT a comparable arm; that happens when only one cell had work.
